knowledge.statement: In the captured EPaxos package the value a recovery adopts is not protected by the quorum that holds it: four distinct mechanisms of the same recovery path each let a recovering replica end up proposing, and then deciding, a value other than the one its prepare replies carry. (a) startRecoveryForInstance fabricates a value ballot for its own state - the recoverer's own id when it is the instance owner and id + N when it is not, without advancing while IsLeader is false - and the adoption loop then honours only replies whose value ballot is at least that fabricated one, so a non-owner recoverer's fabricated ballot sits above the peers' stored value ballots and its genuine replies are skipped (measured: replies at value ballot 0 were passed over against a fabricated ballot of 8), while an owner recovering its own instance fabricates its own id, which equals the peers' value ballot, so their replies are still adopted - the case (d) depends on (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451, 1145-1165, 1239-1246). (b) A reply whose value ballot is below the running candidate ballot - which begins at the recoverer's pre-recovery local value ballot and rises to the fabricated recovery ballot as the loop adopts - is ignored even when it reports the highest accepted value, so a NOOP replaces an accepted value, including one another live replica has already committed; a reply whose value ballot equals the running candidate is still adopted, which is what lets an empty reply replace the command in (d). (c) A reply that reports the instance COMMITTED is discarded once its status reaches lb.status, because the pre-accept guard then rejects the remaining replies, so the first recovery attempt stalls until the retry (epaxos/epaxos.go:870-881, 1255-1313). (d) A reply that carries no command decodes as a non-nil empty slice, which the sub-case 5/6 fallback passes to startPhase1 instead of state.NOOP() (epaxos/defs.go:228-235, epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1311), and the adopted value is the one carried by the last reply appended before the appended count reaches SlowQuorumSize - the fabricated self reply counts toward that threshold, so the trigger falls on the second delivered peer reply and the dispatch then replaces the bookkeeping, so replies delivered afterwards cannot restore the command; the owner's command therefore survives exactly when that second peer reply carries it, measured on one fixed reply set with two command-carrying and two empty peer replies as kept for the orders 1,2,3,4 and 3,1,4,2 and dropped for 1,3,4,2 and 3,4,1,2. Recovering replicas that already hold the value are not affected by (a)-(b), and the client re-offer protects the single-NOOP case but not the empty-slice case.

knowledge.statement: makeBallot assigns the instance owner the ballot equal to its own replica id and any other recovering replica id+N, and advances it in steps of N only while r.IsLeader is true and the candidate is below maxRecvBallot; epaxos.New hardcodes IsLeader false and only the exported BeTheLeader RPC sets it, which the master invokes for the replica it designates. Repeating startRecoveryForInstance without that flag therefore reuses the identical ballot, whereas after the flag is set the same call emits a ballot above maxRecvBallot. For a non-owner, the boundary is the comparison between its fixed id+N ballot and the ballot the accepting peers have stored: id+N below that value is rejected inertly exactly as the owner's ballot is, while id+N above it is joined by the peers and the attempt advances.

knowledge.statement: A nil command slice does not stay nil across the wire: PrepareReply.Unmarshal (and the other RPC decoders) allocate the received slice with make([]state.Command, alen1), so a sender that carries no command yields a non-nil empty slice at the receiver. In handlePrepareReply's adoption loop that empty slice is copied into lb.cmds, and the sub-case 5/6 fallback tests only `inst.lb.cmds != nil`, so it passes the empty slice to startPhase1 instead of substituting state.NOOP(); the resulting instance holds an empty (non-nil) command list, which executeCommands accepts because its guard is also a nil test, and handleCommit's re-offer path does not recognise it because that path requires exactly one command with operation NONE. Which command is adopted is the one carried by the last reply appended before len(lb.prepareReplies) reaches SlowQuorumSize; the recoverer's own fabricated reply is already appended, so with one self reply the trigger falls on the second delivered peer reply, and the dispatch hands the instance to startPhase1 with fresh bookkeeping, so replies delivered after the trigger are appended to that new bookkeeping and never enter the decision. Measured on one fixed reply set with two command-carrying and two empty peer replies, the owner's command survives exactly when the reply at that trigger position carries it - kept for the delivery orders 1,2,3,4 and 3,1,4,2, dropped for 1,3,4,2 and 3,4,1,2 - so neither the first delivered reply nor the number of command-carrying replies decides the outcome. Replies delivered after the trigger cannot re-open the decision, and not only because the instance status has already moved: the dispatch consumes the bookkeeping, the fresh bookkeeping startPhase1 installs begins with no appended replies (measured as lb_appended 0 right after the trigger and 1, then 2, as the two post-trigger replies of the four-reply runs land in it), and the replies that can still arrive after the trigger number N - SlowQuorumSize, which for every N is smaller than SlowQuorumSize itself, so a second dispatch on that bookkeeping is unreachable in this path rather than merely unobserved.

knowledge.statement: A nil command slice does not stay nil across the wire: PrepareReply.Unmarshal (and the other RPC decoders) allocate the received slice with make([]state.Command, alen1), so a sender that carries no command yields a non-nil empty slice at the receiver. In handlePrepareReply's adoption loop that empty slice is copied into lb.cmds, and the sub-case 5/6 fallback tests only `inst.lb.cmds != nil`, so it passes the empty slice to startPhase1 instead of substituting state.NOOP(); the resulting instance holds an empty (non-nil) command list, which executeCommands accepts because its guard is also a nil test, and handleCommit's re-offer path does not recognise it because that path requires exactly one command with operation NONE. Which command is adopted is the one carried by the last reply appended before len(lb.prepareReplies) reaches SlowQuorumSize; the recoverer's own fabricated reply is already appended, so with one self reply the trigger falls on the second delivered peer reply, and the dispatch hands the instance to startPhase1 with fresh bookkeeping, so replies delivered after the trigger are appended to that new bookkeeping and never enter the decision. Measured on one fixed reply set with two command-carrying and two empty peer replies, the owner's command survives exactly when the reply at that trigger position carries it - kept for the delivery orders 1,2,3,4 and 3,1,4,2, dropped for 1,3,4,2 and 3,4,1,2 - so neither the first delivered reply nor the number of command-carrying replies decides the outcome. Replies delivered after the trigger cannot re-open the decision, and not only because the instance status has already moved: the dispatch consumes the bookkeeping, the fresh bookkeeping startPhase1 installs begins with no appended replies (measured as lb_appended 0 right after the trigger and 1, then 2, as the two post-trigger replies of the four-reply runs land in it), and the replies that can still arrive after the trigger number N - SlowQuorumSize, which for every N is smaller than SlowQuorumSize itself, so a second dispatch on that bookkeeping is unreachable in this path rather than merely unobserved.
